# PS5 HD Camera for PC

> A free, open-source (GPL-3.0) driver that makes the PlayStation 5 HD Camera (model CFI-ZEY1) a regular webcam on a PC: native 1920x1080 at 60 fps and background blur (bokeh) from real stereo depth computed on the GPU, on Windows 11, with Linux (bokeh experimental, Vulkan) and macOS (no bokeh) support.

Key facts:

- Hardware: only the PlayStation 5 HD Camera (CFI-ZEY1). It plugs into a regular USB 3 port; no adapter is needed. On USB 2.0 it only delivers 640x400. The PS4 camera is a different device and is not supported, even through a USB adapter.
- Windows 11: the camera appears as "PS5 Camera" in Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Discord, Telegram, OBS Studio, browsers and the Camera app (Media Foundation, WinRT, DirectShow). Install: download PS5CameraDriver.msi (English) or PS5CameraDriver-ru.msi (Russian) from https://github.com/KROU4/PS5CameraDriver/releases/latest and run it; unattended, from an administrator prompt: `msiexec /i PS5CameraDriver.msi /qn BOKEH=on|off`. A winget package `KROU4.PS5CameraDriver` is under review.
- Bokeh without neural networks: depth from the camera's two sensors (census transform + semi-global matching) in Direct3D 11 shaders; the whole head stays sharp (silhouette from depth), with bokeh on, exposure is metered on the person's head, motion-compensated noise reduction and automatic anti-flicker help in dim rooms. It is switched like Windows' own camera effects: Settings → Bluetooth & devices → Cameras → PS5 Camera → Camera effects.
- How it works on Windows: no kernel code and no test mode. A service uploads the camera firmware through Windows' built-in WinUSB; the camera then re-connects as a standard UVC camera; a Device MFT inside Windows Camera Frame Server does the GPU processing.
- Firmware: the camera needs firmware every time it is plugged in. Sony's firmware is not redistributed: the installer downloads the original image from third-party copies on GitHub, checks its SHA-256 and applies a 90-byte patch (1080p at 60 fps, a depth mode, automatic exposure). On Windows an installation without internet access still completes and the service fetches the firmware later; on Linux and macOS the installer needs internet access or the original placed next to it as sony-firmware.bin.
- Performance (RTX 3060 Ti, 1920x1080 at 60 fps): 2.6–2.9 ms GPU time per frame without effects, 8.6–9.0 ms with bokeh; about 60 MB / 100–130 MB of GPU memory. On Windows a GPU with Direct3D 11 is required, integrated graphics count (Vulkan 1.1 for the Linux bokeh); the plain camera on Linux and macOS needs no GPU.
- Linux: `sudo bash install.sh` from PS5CameraDriver-linux.zip (systemd and udev required); the camera is "USB Camera-OV580". `--bokeh on` adds the experimental bokeh as a v4l2loopback camera "PS5 Camera" (x86_64 with glibc 2.34+, Vulkan 1.1; the installer installs the v4l2loopback kernel module, with Secure Boot its key must be enrolled).
- macOS: `sudo bash install.sh` from PS5CameraDriver-macos.zip (Command Line Tools required); 1080p at 30/60 fps without bokeh; the camera is "USB Camera-OV580".
- Limitations: one program uses the camera at a time; depth is measured from about half a metre.
- Not affiliated with Sony Interactive Entertainment. PlayStation and PS5 are trademarks of Sony Interactive Entertainment Inc.

## Docs

- [Website (English)](https://krou4.github.io/PS5CameraDriver/): overview, install, performance, FAQ
- [Website (Russian)](https://krou4.github.io/PS5CameraDriver/ru/): the same in Russian
- [README](https://github.com/KROU4/PS5CameraDriver/blob/main/README.md): full description, firmware patch, architecture, building from source
- [Windows install and troubleshooting](https://github.com/KROU4/PS5CameraDriver/blob/main/installer/README.txt): modes, settings, ps5cam-ctl commands
- [Linux install](https://github.com/KROU4/PS5CameraDriver/blob/main/installer/linux/README.txt): plain camera and Vulkan bokeh

## Downloads

- [Latest release](https://github.com/KROU4/PS5CameraDriver/releases/latest): MSI and ZIP for Windows, Linux and macOS packages
- [Source code](https://github.com/KROU4/PS5CameraDriver): GPL-3.0

## Optional

- [Firmware patch](https://github.com/KROU4/PS5CameraDriver/blob/main/firmware/ps5cam-firmware.json): the original firmware hash, its public sources and the byte changes
